summary_html: **CAPTA §5106a(c)** requires every state to maintain **Citizen Review Panels** that evaluate CPS policies. Project Milk Carton checks whether panels are active, independent, and publicly reporting.
authority_html: - **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. § 5106a(c))** — Citizen Review Panel mandate and reporting requirements

District of Columbia - D.C. Code Title 4, Chapter 13, Subchapter I, Part C-ii (Citizen Review Panel) — §§ 4-1303.51 to 4-1303.55

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: United States District Court for the District of Columbia
key_cases.holding: After trial the court found the District's child welfare system violated federal and District statutory and constitutional requirements at nearly every stage, including a consistent failure to provide services or make reasonable efforts to prevent placement, and ordered systemic relief.
key_cases.relevance: It illustrates why independent external review of District CPS policy has been necessary.
key_cases.quote: the Court finds that defendants have consistently failed to provide services or otherwise use “reasonable efforts” to prevent placement

key_cases.court: District of Columbia Court of Appeals
key_cases.holding: When CPS receives a report identifying particular children as abused, the Child Abuse Prevention Act creates a special relationship imposing on the District a duty to take the steps the Act prescribes for those children, so summary judgment for the District was error.
key_cases.relevance: It shows that the statutory duties a citizen review panel evaluates are judicially enforceable obligations, not aspirations.
key_cases.quote: From that moment on, the District had a duty to take certain steps prescribed by the Act for the protection of those children.

key_cases.case_name: Vining v. Council of the District of Columbia
key_cases.court: District of Columbia Court of Appeals
key_cases.holding: The Council may not invoke the Legislative Privilege Act through D.C. FOIA Exemption 6 (or, on this record, Exemption 4) to withhold documents responsive to a FOIA request, and summary judgment for the Council was reversed.
key_cases.relevance: It supports the ability of citizen reviewers to obtain the District records they need to evaluate CPS policy.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the Legislative Privilege Act cannot be invoked through Exemption 6 so as to permit the Council to withhold documents responsive to a FOIA request

timeline_requirements.deadline: Immediately if MPD deems the child critical missing; otherwise once the child has been missing more than 30 days (MPD makes the NCMEC report)
timeline_requirements.starts_from: CFSA files a missing person report with MPD immediately after discovering the child is missing (D.C. Code § 4-1323.01(a))
